solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rob in Edinburgh being shown round small flat, perhaps

indicators.note: a visitor being shown round is led all the way around a place, so the Scots word wraps all the way around the French one

parts.note: reive is Scots for rob or plunder, hence the Border reivers

explanation.surface: A burglar in Edinburgh cases a small flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' is not a home but a tone of voice: a flat, repetitive delivery. The 'perhaps' warns the definition is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a flat, monotonous voice or style is one kind of repetitive thing, never varying.

clue.text: Clergymen always in tears

indicators.note: something that is in something else sits inside it

explanation.surface: Men of the cloth who are forever weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' reads as weeping; here it is the verb tear, to rip.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: Reverend is the title given to clergy, so reverends is an everyday name for clergymen.

clue.text: City district losing hospital

indicators.note: a word that is losing something has it taken away

parts.note: H = hospital, as on road signs; removed

explanation.surface: A city neighbourhood whose hospital has closed.
explanation.walkthrough: H for hospital comes from the blue road-sign letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the French capital is one instance of a city.

clue.text: Task in surveying awfully unoriginal tat

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, and badly arranged letters are out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A critic dismissing a surveyor's work as derivative junk.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is the whole of 'unoriginal tat'; 'awfully' reads as an intensifier but mixes the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Surveyors fix positions by measuring the angles of a network of triangles; that job is called triangulation.

clue.text: End of fish after lake is become tainted

indicators.note: after places the final letter behind the lake and is in the answer

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of fish is used

explanation.surface: A fish taken from a lake goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarnish is to lose lustre or become discoloured, so to be spoiled or tainted.

clue.text: Throbbing effect of old instrument nearly broken by bad child

indicators.note: the instrument is split open with the child put in the gap
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the viol is an early bowed string instrument
a brat is a badly behaved child

explanation.surface: A naughty child damages an antique instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken by' reads as damage, but it means the shortened instrument is split open to take the child.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibrato is a regular pulsing variation in pitch used by singers and string players.

clue.text: Leave out leading role not quite recalled?

indicators.note: not quite the whole word means it stops one letter short
called back: the word is brought back the way it came, read from end to start

parts.note: Timon, title role of Shakespeare's Timon of Athens, minus N

explanation.surface: An actor dropped from the lead after half-remembering the part.
explanation.walkthrough: A leading role is a title role; the question mark flags that Timon is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to leave something out of a list is to omit it.

clue.text: Trail ringing university that's some distance outside US city

indicators.note: to ring something is to form a ring around it
what stands outside another thing encloses it

parts.note: a wake is the trail left by a boat

explanation.surface: A hiking trail around a campus some way out of an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: U inside WAKE, and that inside MI…LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Milwaukee, the Wisconsin brewing city, is one US city.

clue.text: Bear eating last of layer cake

indicators.note: what is eaten ends up inside the eater

parts.note: to tote is to carry, to bear

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A bear tucking into a layer cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' is the animal in the picture, but the verb in the wordplay: carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich Central European kind of cake, often built in layers.

clue.text: Virtual reality encapsulates computer that does drawing in fine scale

indicators.note: to encapsulate is to enclose as if in a capsule

parts.note: ERNIE is the machine that picks Premium Bond winners

explanation.surface: A headset simulation containing a computer used for sketching.
explanation.walkthrough: The drawing is a prize draw, not a picture: ERNIE draws the winning numbers of Premium Bonds, a British state savings lottery.
explanation.definitionFit: A vernier is a small sliding auxiliary scale that reads a main scale to fine fractions, as on calipers.

clue.text: Pub opened up by Ripon's centre lures initially like a magnet

indicators.note: opened up by means the pub word is split with other letters put inside
centre means the middle letters of Ripon are used, dropping its ends

parts.note: Ripon is a cathedral city in Yorkshire; the apostrophe s is the possessive

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of lures is used

explanation.surface: A pub in the middle of Ripon draws customers in like a magnet.
explanation.walkthrough: Ripon is a small cathedral city in North Yorkshire; its centre is its three middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet is bipolar, having two poles, north and south, at opposite ends.

clue.text: What royal needs to succeed, proper routine, eg being ordered

indicators.note: being ordered means put into a fresh order, so routine and eg are rearranged

explanation.surface: A royal heir needs a proper routine to take the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being ordered' turns ROUTINEEG into OGENITURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Primogeniture is the rule of inheritance by the firstborn, which decides who succeeds to a throne.

clue.text: Note second king's essential offering is frankincense?

parts.note: re, the second note of do-re-mi

indicators.note: the essential part of something is its core, so take the middle two letters of king

parts.note: the middle two letters of king

explanation.surface: The second of the Three Kings brings his frankincense.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the Nativity gift; the question mark marks frankincense as one example of a resin.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: frankincense is the dried aromatic gum of the Boswellia tree, one kind of resin.

clue.text: One granny and current companion, not quick

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A slow old granny with her companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' is the old sense, alive, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick in its archaic sense means living, so something not quick is lifeless, inanimate.

clue.text: Unfair criticism of tiny museum?

definitions.meaning: the everyday idiom: a dismissive remark that someone is plain or unattractive
the literal reading: a very small museum has few exhibits to see

explanation.surface: A reviewer being harsh on a very small museum.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means plain or unattractive, which is unfair criticism; read literally, a tiny museum has few exhibits.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: calling someone not much to look at disparages their looks, but a tiny museum literally has few things to see.

clue.text: Poem with a message is surprisingly select hit

indicators.note: letters that come out surprisingly land in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A poem with a moral that turned into an unexpected hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The message is spelt out, not preached: the hidden word is in the last letters of the lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A telestich is a poem whose line endings spell a word, so it literally carries a hidden message.

clue.text: Turn on appeal badly introduced by gallery

indicators.note: introduced by means taken into, so the gallery holds the other letters

parts.note: the Tate is a group of art galleries in Britain
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A gallery introducing a poorly made appeal to arouse interest.
explanation.walkthrough: IT, for sex appeal, is a crossword convention. IT + ILL go inside TATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to excite or arouse someone, often sexually, which is to turn them on.

clue.text: One's getting on running famed clan events

indicators.note: letters that are running are on the move, so they will not stay in their printed order

explanation.surface: An aging clansman still running in the famous Highland games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting on' reads as growing old; here it is getting ahead, and 'One's' makes it on your own behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on means getting ahead in life; one's own getting ahead is self-advancement.

clue.text: Evil genius saving notes for capital

indicators.note: saving in its old sense of except, as in 'all saving one', so everything is kept but the notes

parts.note: the musical notes E, G, E are removed

explanation.surface: A villain rescuing banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving' means except, not rescuing; strip the notes E, G and E and what remains reads straight through in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Vilnius is the capital city of Lithuania.

clue.text: Managed overturning estimate in recount

indicators.note: to overturn is to turn upside down, and in a down clue that means the word reads backwards

explanation.surface: Officials overturning an estimate during a vote recount.
explanation.walkthrough: The recount sounds like an election but is the verb: to tell a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Recount as a verb means tell the story of, which is to narrate.

clue.text: Drinks manufacturer's unit not so active following end of Covid

indicators.note: what is following comes behind
the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A drinks firm's plant has been quieter since the pandemic.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Distillers make spirits such as whisky and gin, so a distiller is a drinks manufacturer.

clue.text: Stage design has company surrounded by rising colour

indicators.note: a thing surrounded by another is enclosed on all sides
in a down clue, a word rising reads from the bottom up, backwards

explanation.surface: A theatre company's set, bathed in a rising glow of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' works only because this is a down clue: the colour is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In the theatre, décor is the scenery and furnishing of the stage, its design.

clue.text: Drive MP out with lie

indicators.note: out as in out of order or put out: the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Force out a politician caught lying.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants 'drive out' as a phrase; split it, and 'Drive' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to impel is to drive or urge forward.

clue.text: Parents taking in Republican city

indicators.note: to take someone in is to give them a place inside

explanation.surface: Parents putting up a Republican in their city.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the last word; 'Parents' is two words' worth, pa and ma.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Parma, home of the ham and the cheese, is a city in northern Italy.

clue.text: A little gnocchi, antipasto and wine

indicators.note: a little of something is only a portion, so the answer is a stretch of the following words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the pasta into the start of the starter

explanation.surface: An Italian meal: a few gnocchi, a starter and a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer belongs at the same table as the food that hides it: CHIANTI straddles gnocchi and antipasto.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Chianti is the Tuscan red, one wine among many.

clue.text: A Queen song which may contain lots of bass

definitions.text: which may contain lots of bass

parts.note: Qu = queen, as in card and chess shorthand
an aria is an operatic song

explanation.surface: A song by the band Queen with a heavy bass line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen song' points to the rock band and 'bass' to the guitar; the bass is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquaria are fish tanks, and bass are fish, so a descriptive definition of what they can hold.

clue.text: Regularly rougher mining area

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so take letters at an even step, every other one

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A mining district that is usually the rougher one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' reads as usually, but it is telling you to pick letters at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Ruhr in western Germany was Europe's great coal-mining region.

clue.text: Maintain a cut during glut

indicators.note: what happens during something falls within it, so the cut sits inside the glut

parts.note: to sate is to glut, to fill to excess

explanation.surface: Keeping a price cut going while the market is flooded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maintain' here means declare firmly, not keep up.
explanation.definitionFit: Maintain in the sense of insist that something is true; asseverate is the formal word for that solemn assertion.
